message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t give you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s what you can do to find the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow.gov** | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code to see the current AQI, pollutant breakdowns, and forecast. |
| **EPA Air Quality Index Mobile App** | Download the app (iOS/Android) for push notifications and quick checks. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Many local outlets publish daily air‑quality summaries. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Some include AQI data in their weather reports. |

Typical AQI categories (0–500) are:

- 0–50 : Good  
- 51–100 : Moderate  
- 101–150 : Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  
- 151–200 : Unhealthy  
- 201–300 : Very Unhealthy  
- 301–500 : Hazardous  

If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s best to check the current AQI and any health advisories. If you need help interpreting the numbers or want to know how to protect yourself when the AQI is high, let me know!
